rounds.plan: Head forward along the open corridor to explore for the green beacon, then reassess.
Mirror wall directly ahead blocked forward. Turn right and move along the open lane.
Forward and right are blocked; try the left-facing direction.
Open lane ahead. Advance down the corridor, then turn right and continue to sweep for the green beacon.
Dead end ahead. Turn 180 to back out of the pocket, then explore the perpendicular opening to the left.
Explore southward from current cell: turn right and advance until blocked or the beacon appears.
Front is a mirror wall (own reflection). Turn left and take the side corridor.
Boxed in facing mirrors. Turn 180 degrees and backtrack the way we came to find an opening.
Corridor still appears open ahead (reflection far). Advance two cells, then turn left to sweep the side lane.
Wall directly ahead (mirror reflection). Turn left into the open lane and advance to search for the beacon.
Forward is a mirror wall (own reflection fills the view). Turn left and advance along the open side lane to search for the green beacon.
Dead-end pocket facing a mirror. Reverse out to the previous cell, then turn into the unexplored perpendicular branch.
Facing a mirror dead end. Reverse one cell to the junction, then turn right into the unexplored branch and advance.
Facing a mirror wall. Adopt right-hand wall following: turn right and step, repeating to trace around obstacles toward unexplored cells.
Open hall ahead with no beacon in view. Advance down the corridor, then sweep a side branch.
Dead-end mirror ahead. Reverse direction and take the unexplored side branch to the left.
Backtrack to (0,1) junction and push west into the unexplored lane to look for the green beacon.
Front blocked by a mirror wall. Turn 180 to face the unexplored perpendicular direction and advance.
Facing a mirror wall (own reflection). Rotate left to the perpendicular lane and advance two cells to test that branch.
Facing a close mirror wall. Turn right and advance along the open lane, probing for side openings and the green beacon.
This heading is blocked by a mirror wall. Rotate to the opposite direction (west) which is likely open, and advance along that corridor.
Mirror wall directly ahead (own reflection). Turn left into the perpendicular lane and advance two cells to probe it.
Confirmed: the centered mirror image means a mirror wall is directly ahead. The left side looks clear while the right shows another close mirror. Turn left and advance along the open lane.
Mirror wall directly ahead with another mirror close on the left; the right side looks open. Turn right and advance down that lane.
Mirror directly ahead. Begin right-hand wall following in long segments: pivot right and advance, repeating around the loop to trace the boundary and find the beacon.
Boxed in on three sides (forward mirror plus close mirrors left/right). Reverse 180, retrace three cells, then turn left to push into unexplored territory.
Facing a mirror wall. Rotate left and test one step into that lane to see the actual geometry.
Confirmed mirror wall ahead and reflective sides; no visible real beacon. Reverse 180 and back out of this pocket along the corridor we entered from.
Front is a mirror wall. The right-hand corridor looks open and a faint green marker appears that way. Turn right and advance to probe it.
Corridor ahead reads as open; advance three cells and reassess for a real (non-reflected) green beacon.
Blocked ahead by a mirror; a green beacon-like pole shows toward the right. Turn right and advance that way to approach it.
Mirror wall dead ahead (own front reflection). Turn left into the open perpendicular lane and advance to keep exploring.
Mirror wall ahead. Turn 180, back out along the corridor we came from, then turn right and push into the open hall to explore for the real green beacon.
Current heading is blocked and the left side is a close mirror; retreat 180 degrees and move back south along the open corridor.
Turn back to the open-hall heading seen earlier (green markers on that side) and advance through the clear lane.
Facing a mirror pocket. Turn 180 and back out to the junction, then reassess for an open lane.
Turn right toward the green marker down the open lane and advance to approach it.
Facing an adjacent mirror, with a real green beacon visible toward the right. Turn right and advance toward that beacon area.
Mirror wall directly ahead with a close mirror to the right. Turn left into the open lane and advance three cells toward the open hall.
Open mirror hall; no real green beacon in view ahead (only reflections). Turn right and traverse the perpendicular lane to sweep for the beacon.
Facing a mirror wall; the lane along our previous heading was still open. Turn left back onto it and continue advancing.
Mirror wall directly ahead (own reflection), open colonnade to the sides. Turn right and advance along the open lane to sweep for a real green beacon.
Advance down the long open corridor, then turn left toward the side wall where a green panel appeared and continue probing.
Pocket ahead is mirror. Turn right to face the eastern colonnade, advance to test it, and approach the green column visible on that side.
Dead-end pocket with mirrors flanking and ahead. Rotate 180 degrees and move back out along the open corridor.
Continue back along the open corridor two cells, then turn left into a new lane and sweep it for the real green beacon.
Open colonnade ahead; advance along it to the far end, then reassess for a real beacon versus reflections.
Mirror wall ahead blocks forward. Turn left into the open colonnade lane and advance to keep sweeping for the real green beacon.
The cyan floor rings (beacon images) sit to the front-left. Turn left toward the nearest ring and advance to step onto it if real.
The cyan ring at bottom-left is one cell to the west of my current position. Turn left, then step forward onto it to test whether it is the actual beacon.
Pocket: front, left and right are all mirrors; only the way back is open. Reverse 180 degrees and travel back out along the open corridor.
Wall directly ahead. Turn right toward the cyan floor rings on that side and advance to test whether one is the real beacon.
Frontal mirror wall ahead (own chest reflection centered), right side blocked close. Turn left into the open colonnade and advance several cells, then reassess.
Facing a close mirror. Turn left toward the open-looking lane and probe one cell forward.
On a cyan decal; front is a mirror wall. Turn right into the more open eastern lane and advance several cells, scanning for the real green beacon.
Mirror directly ahead; the left side is open floor. Turn left and advance a few cells along that lane to keep searching for the real green beacon.
Facing a mirror wall dead ahead (own reflection centered) with mirrors close on both sides. Reverse direction and back out along the corridor we came from.
Mirror wall ahead. Turn left back onto the open lane we came from and sweep westward to hunt the real beacon.
Wall ahead confirmed (own reflection). The left side reads as open deep space, so turn left and advance along that corridor.
Blocked ahead (mirror). Turn right to face the untested northern lane and advance to see if it opens toward the beacon.
Boxed in by mirrors ahead; reverse 180 degrees and retreat along the corridor we arrived through, then try the perpendicular branch.
Front is a mirror wall, but the left colonnade lane reads open. Turn left and push along it three cells, then reassess.
Wall directly ahead. Apply right-hand wall following: turn right into the open lane beside me and advance to trace new ground.
Close mirror fills the view (own face). Apply wall-following: pivot right and test forward, pivot right again and test forward to find the open direction.
Open mirror hall; no real green beacon visible yet. Continue forward along this clear lane and reassess.
Facing a mirror wall head-on. Turn left into the clear west lane and advance several cells to search for the real green beacon.
Front is a mirror wall; the cyan floor ring marker sits to the right. Rotate right toward it and advance to test that cell.
Open mirrored hall with many virtual reflections and cyan decals; no real green beacon in view. Continue advancing straight along the open central lane to reach new ground, then reassess.
Mirror wall directly ahead. Turn right toward the open right lane with cyan floor rings and advance, then reassess.
Mirror directly ahead. Turn left toward the open lane with the cyan floor rings and advance to keep searching for the real beacon.
Switch to a systematic boustrophedon sweep: reverse to the boundary, then traverse long segments, shifting one lane and reversing, to cover the 7x7 grid.
Facing a mirror wall in the open hall. Turn right and sweep along that lane to cover new ground, then reassess.
The front is a mirror wall (own reflection centered) in a large mirrored hall with open floor to the left. Turn left and advance along that lane, probing for the actual green beacon.
Mirror wall ahead, no real green beacon in view. Sweep systematically in long boustrophedon legs to cover new cells.
Front is a mirror wall in the open hall. Turn left into the clear lane and advance to keep sweeping for the real green beacon.

Vision is overwhelmed by mirror reflections, so switch to a dense deterministic sweep: repeatedly rotate right and drive a long straight leg, packing many actions into one decision to cover the whole grid and step onto the real beacon.
Robot is in a dead-end cell facing a mirror wall. Back up one cell to the junction, then turn into the untried side branch and step in.
Mirror ahead. Reverse 180, back one cell, then turn left and probe the perpendicular lane.
Front blocked. Turn right into the open west lane and advance several cells, watching for a real green beacon (not a cyan ring or reflection).
Mirror directly ahead. Turn left into the open floor lane and drive a long leg, then turn right and sweep the next lane to cover unexplored ground.
Dead end facing a mirror. Reverse 180 to back out of the pocket, then turn into the perpendicular lane and step in.
Large mirrored hall; front blocked. Turn left (west), drive a long leg, turn right and drive the next leg, then turn right again to sweep adjacent lanes covering new ground.
Stuck against a wall in the mirrored hall. Rotate left and drive a long leg in that new direction to reach unexplored cells.
Front and left are mirrors; only the way back is open. Reverse 180 degrees and retreat three cells along the known-open path to reach the junction, then reassess.
Front is a mirror wall. Turn left (west) and drive a long leg along the open lane to reach new ground.
Dead-end pocket with a mirror ahead. Turn left toward the open hall visible on that side and advance several cells to reach new ground.
Blocked by a mirror wall head-on; turn left into the open floor lane and advance a few cells, then reassess.

Mirror hall with no real beacon in view yet. Switch to sustained right-hand wall following in one long packed sequence (4 steps forward, then rotate right, repeated) to trace corridors and eventually sweep onto the actual green beacon cell.
Mirrored hall blocks this heading; turn to an adjacent lane and drive a long leg to reach unexplored cells, then turn again to cover the next lane.
Two opposite headings are blocked. Test the first of the two untested perpendicular headings with a single probe.
Forward lane is open through the glass colonnade; advance several cells and then sweep a side lane to look for the real green beacon.
Front is a mirror wall; open floor with cyan decals lies to the left. Turn left and advance along that lane, then probe the far side for the real green beacon.
Back out of the dead-end cell to the junction (180 then one step), turn south onto the untested heading, and probe forward along it.

Begin a wall-synchronized lawnmower sweep: shift one lane over, then traverse full-length legs alternating direction, one cell apart, to guarantee covering all 7 columns and stepping onto the real green beacon.
Stuck facing a mirror wall; the west lane looks open. Turn left and advance several cells to traverse new corridor and look for the real green beacon.
Mirror wall head-on. Turn right to try the perpendicular lane and drive a long leg, then reassess.
Mirror wall directly ahead and another close on the right; the left lane reads open. Turn left and advance up to four cells along it, re-checking at the next image.
Facing a mirror wall; take the open perpendicular lane. Turn right (north) and advance a few cells, then reassess.
On a cyan decal facing a mirror wall. Turn left into the open perpendicular corridor and advance a few cells to seek the real green beacon.
Facing a mirror wall on a cyan decal. Turn right and probe one cell to test that heading.
Identical view confirms a mirror wall ahead on all probed headings. Exhaust a square-tracing sweep: about-face, then long legs with quarter-turns to cover new ground in this mirrored hall.
Mirror wall ahead; the west lane shows open floor with a distant red marker. Turn left and advance along it to reach new cells.
Two adjacent headings are walled off. Turn to the next untested heading and advance several cells through it.
Mirror directly west. Turn left to face south and advance up to four cells along the open lane until a wall stops us.
No visible non-reflected green beacon; use a long randomized wandering pattern with varied leg lengths and turns so the walker covers many cells and lands on the actual beacon cell.
All three facing sides are mirrors; only the way back is open. About-face and retreat along the open corridor, then shift lanes to cover unexplored cells.
A mirror wall sits directly ahead (the hall seen ahead is a reflection of the space behind). Turn into the open side lane and zigzag to limit repeated wall hits.
Mirror wall directly ahead again. Turn right into the side lane and probe a single cell.
Mirror walls box in the front and both flanks here. About-face and retreat along the corridor we came from, two cells back to open floor.
Centered full self-reflection = mirror wall directly ahead. Turn toward the open lane with the cyan floor rings and probe one cell.
Self-reflection fills the frame again — mirror wall ahead. Try the right-hand side lane with a single probe.
Only the way we came is open — front, left, and right all block. About-face and back out of this pocket.
Wall (mirror) directly ahead — the centered self-reflection confirms it. Rotate into the open right-hand lane and probe one cell.
Large centered self-reflection one cell ahead — mirror wall blocks forward. Turn right into the open colonnade lane and probe a single cell.
Immediate mirror wall ahead — the oversized centered self-reflection confirms it. This time swing left into the lane with the pink floor markers and probe one cell.
Open colonnade ahead with receding floor frames (mirrors far off, not adjacent). Advance along the lane, then turn right into the next aisle and continue sweeping.
Centered full-size self-reflection one cell ahead — a mirror wall blocks this heading (the 'hall' ahead is a reflection). Rotate right into the perpendicular aisle and probe a single cell.
Centered full-size self-reflection one cell ahead — a mirror wall blocks this heading. Turn left into the perpendicular aisle and probe a single cell.
Front, left, and right all mirror-blocked. About-face and step back a single cell, then reassess.
Front and both flanks are mirror-blocked; the only open route is back the way we came. About-face toward the corridor behind (right), then retreat two cells along it.
A huge centered self-reflection sits one cell ahead — mirror wall dead ahead. Turn right into the open floor and sweep a lane, then quarter-turn left to change aisle.
All three facing directions are mirror walls; only the rear is open. About-face and retreat along the corridor with cyan floor rings, then turn left into a new aisle and probe.
Mirror wall dead ahead (centered self-reflection); the right flank is also mirrored close in. Turn left into the open colonnade with the pink floor decals and probe one cell.
Lane ahead looks clear for a couple of cells before the mirror plane. Advance two cells, quarter-turn left, and probe two more to change aisle.
Centered full-size self-reflection one cell ahead confirms a mirror wall on this heading. Turn right into the clear lane beside the pink floor decals and probe a single cell.
Centered self-reflection one cell ahead again — mirror wall. Both forward headings here are blocked, so swing to the opposite side lane and probe a single cell.
The central reflection marks a mirror plane ahead. Turn left into the open aisle beside the pink floor arrows and advance two cells.
The self-reflection is huge and centered — a mirror wall sits immediately ahead. Turn right into the side aisle and probe one cell only.
Own reflection fills the center at arm's length and both flanks are mirrored — a dead-end pocket. About-face, retreat three cells along the corridor that was open, then turn right and probe one cell.
The centered self-reflection again shows a mirror wall immediately ahead. Turn right into the side aisle and probe a single cell to avoid stacked wall hits.
Open colonnade ahead — receding frames with only distant small reflections, no near mirror plane. Advance three cells, quarter-turn left into the next aisle, and continue two more.
Mirror wall immediately ahead again; the near reflection on the right shows that flank is also mirrored. Only the route back is open, so about-face left and retreat along the corridor.
Mirror wall right in front (full-size centered self-reflection). Turn left into the side aisle and probe a single cell to avoid stacked wall hits.

Mirror plane immediately ahead (oversized centered self-reflection); the near reflection on the right marks that flank as mirrored too. Turn left into the clear aisle with the pink floor markers and probe one cell.
Centered full-size self-reflection one cell ahead, with large close reflections on both flanks — a mirror pocket. About-face and back out along the open corridor, then reassess.
Full-size centered self-reflection one cell ahead — a mirror wall blocks this heading. Turn right into the side aisle and probe a single cell only, to avoid stacking wall hits.
After the step, a large centered self-reflection sits one cell ahead — mirror wall on this heading. Turn left toward the pink floor decal lane and probe one cell.

Forward and the left heading are both mirror-blocked; the near oversized reflection on the right marks that flank as mirrored too. About-face (left) and retreat along the open corridor we came from, two cells.
Full-frontal self-reflection at arm's length — mirror wall directly ahead, flanks mirrored too. About-face and step back one cell, then reassess.
Mirror wall still one cell ahead (full-frontal self-reflection). Swing left into the long open perspective lane and travel several cells, then quarter-turn right to open a new aisle.
Front blocked at this heading as well, so the only open route is the rearward corridor. About-face and retreat two cells, then reassess from the new observation.
A full-frame self-reflection sits one cell ahead, and a close oversized reflection fills the right edge — front and right are mirrored. Turn left into the only open lane and probe a single cell.
Own visor/chest fills the center at close range — a mirror wall sits directly ahead. Turn right into the open lane with the pink floor markers and probe a single cell.
Turning right landed facing another immediate mirror wall. Reverse that turn — swing left instead and probe a single cell in the opposite lane.
Dead-end pocket: the mirror wall sits directly in front, flanked by reflections. About-face, retreat two cells, then quarter-turn right and probe one cell to test a perpendicular branch.
Reflection of the robot's own chest sits centered half a frame ahead — mirror plane on this heading. Turn left toward the open floor with cyan ring decals and probe a single cell.
The mirror plane is directly ahead (full frontal self-reflection, arm's length). Only the lateral lane is open: rotate right and probe a single cell.
Full-body self-reflection fills the center one cell ahead, and a close mirrored self is clipped at the left edge — a dead-end pocket. About-face and retreat along the open corridor behind.
The reflection is only the pillar-field self-image, not a wall at my feet — the hall is broadly open ahead. March a staircase pattern (advance two, quarter-turn right) to sweep new aisles quickly.

Surrounded by a dense mirror lattice; repeated multi-forward batches keep stacking wall hits. Instead probe all four headings cheaply — alternate quarter-turn with a single forward — so at most one cell of the pocket is wasted.
Probing all four headings confirmed only one opening, and it lies directly behind. Right-hand wall following from here: about-face, then advance until the corridor bends, probing two cells at a time.
Centered self-reflection fills the frame one cell ahead — mirror pillar dead ahead. Turn left into the open side aisle and advance two cells to clear the pillar line.

Turn left again points straight into a mirror wall (full-size central self-reflection). About-face, back out two cells along the open corridor, then quarter-turn right and probe one cell into the side branch.

Open colonnade with receding frames and only distant self-images — no mirror plane at arm's length. The cyan ring decals lie to the left, so advance two cells along the aisle, quarter-turn left, and continue two more toward that lane.

Forward is blocked by a mirror wall at arm's length (full-size central self-reflection, ring decal mirrored under its feet). The right-hand lane with the cyan ring decal looks open — turn right and advance two cells along it.
Full-frontal self-reflection at arm's length again — mirror wall dead ahead. Apply right-hand wall following: quarter-turn right and probe a single cell only, so a miss costs just one collision.

The self-reflection ahead is full-frame, so a mirror wall sits one cell in front, and the clipped self-image on the left marks that flank as mirrored too. The right colonnade reads open (distant, small copies only) — turn right and probe a single cell.

After stepping forward, a full-frame self-reflection fills the center at close range — mirror wall directly ahead, and the clipped large reflection on the right marks that flank as mirrored too. Turn left into the remaining open lane and probe a single cell.

Broad open hall with only distant pillar reflections — no mirror plane at arm's length. Run a lawnmower sweep to cover ground quickly: long leg forward, quarter-turn right, one cell across, quarter-turn right, long leg back.

Front is mirror-blocked; the close chest reflection clipped at the left edge marks that flank as pillar too. Swing right into the clearer side lane with the cyan floor rings and roll two cells if open.

Mirror wall fills the center at arm's length; the clipped full-size reflection at the right edge shows that flank is mirrored too. The left lane past the half-height panel with the cyan rings looks clear — turn left and probe one cell.

The figure on the cyan ring ahead is my own mirror image standing at arm's length — a mirror plane blocks this heading, and the clipped large reflection on the right marks that flank too. The left vista is long and open with only distant copies, so swing left and advance three cells along it.
The centered full-size self-reflection at arm's length confirms a mirror wall directly ahead; repeated forwards only add collisions. Turn right into the side lane and probe a single cell.

A full-size centered self-reflection sits at arm's length — mirror wall dead ahead, and the large clipped reflection on the left marks that flank as mirrored too. The right colonnade recedes open, so turn right, probe one cell, then quarter-turn right again and probe once more to test the perpendicular lane without stacking wall hits.
The quarter-turn right put me face-to-face with a mirror wall (full-frame centered self-reflection). Undo that turn and continue down the long open colonnade that ran ahead before the turn.
Dead-end niche: the mirror wall is one cell ahead and the flank at the previous cell is closed too. About-face, step back to the junction cell, then turn left (south) and probe that branch twice.
Blocked facing this mirror pillar. Undo the turn and retrace the open corridor behind me, advancing several cells to regain the clear pillar field.
Arm's-length self-reflection blocks this heading. A long open colonnade runs off to the side, so swing right and advance along it to reach new ground.

A full-size self-reflection fills the center at arm's length — mirror wall directly ahead, and the large clipped self-image at the left edge marks that flank as mirrored too. Turn right into the remaining lane and probe a single cell.
Open pillar field ahead — the centered self-image is several cells off, not an arm's-length wall. Advance two cells along the aisle, quarter-turn left, then two more along the new lane.
Front and left are both mirror-blocked; the rear corridor is the only open route. About-face to the south lane, retreat two cells, then reassess from open floor.
Now the reflection fills the frame at arm's length — mirror wall one cell ahead. The left lane past the cyan ring looks open, so turn left and probe a single cell to avoid stacking wall hits.

The centered chest-and-visor reflection sits at arm's length with a second large clipped one at the right edge — front and right are mirror walls. Turn left into the long open colonnade with the cyan floor rings and advance two cells.
Arm's-length self-reflection confirms the mirror wall dead ahead. Undo the west probe and swing into the east lane, probing one cell at a time so a miss costs only one collision.

Full-frame centered self-reflection at arm's length plus a large clipped reflection on the right — front and right are mirror walls. The left colonnade looks open, so turn left and probe a single cell.
Open pillar hall ahead with only distant copies of the robot — no arm's-length mirror plane. Advance two cells, quarter-turn right into the next aisle, and continue two more to cover new ground.
Forward and the left flank are both mirror planes, but the right-hand colonnade with the cyan ring decals reads open. Quarter-turn right and probe a single cell, then reassess.

This heading runs through an open pillar field — the centered self-image is several cells off, not at arm's length. Advance two cells, quarter-turn left, then two more along the new lane to cover fresh ground.

Current heading is a mirror plane (centered full frontal self-reflection), right flank is mirrored too, but the left vista with the pink floor markers recedes open. Turn left, run three cells, quarter-turn left, then two more to sweep new ground.

At arm's length the centered self-reflection means a mirror wall dead ahead, with the large clipped copy at the right edge showing that flank is mirrored too. The left vista recedes open with only distant copies, so turn left and probe one cell.
Full-frame self-reflection at arm's length — mirror wall dead ahead. Swing right into the open perpendicular lane and probe a single cell.

Full-frame centered self-reflection at arm's length: a mirror wall sits directly ahead on this heading too, so front and the previously tried turn are both blocked. About-face and retreat along the corridor behind, then reassess.
Self-reflection at arm's length ahead, and the big clipped copy at the right edge shows that flank is mirrored too — so the left lane is the only open route. Turn left, then probe two cells along it.

Arm's-length self-reflection dead ahead with a large clipped mirror copy at the left edge, so only the right lane is open. Quarter-turn right, roll two cells down that open aisle, then quarter-turn right again and take two more to swing around the mirror plane.
The centered self-image is near but still off by a cell; the right-hand lane with the cyan ring decals recedes open. Quarter-turn right and roll two cells along it, then reassess.

Arm's-length self-reflection dead ahead confirms a mirror wall, with a clipped large copy on the right marking that flank mirrored too. The left vista with the cyan ring decals recedes open, so turn left and advance two cells.

My own front-facing reflection stands on a cyan ring one cell ahead — a mirror plane blocks this heading (the blue back-view copy at the right is a reflection of my rear). Turn right and probe a single cell so a miss costs just one collision.
Own front-facing reflection stands on a cyan ring one cell ahead — mirror plane on this heading as well. About-face and retreat two cells along the corridor behind, then reassess.
Own visor at arm's length — mirror wall dead ahead. Turn back toward the open corridor we just came down and travel three cells, then reassess.
The centered self-reflection shows the mirror plane still on this heading. The floor to the left of it is open with cyan ring decals receding, so swing left into that aisle and roll two cells.

Mirror plane one cell ahead (centered full-frontal self-reflection); left flank also mirrored. Front blocked, left blocked — the right-hand lane beside the pillars looks open. Turn right and probe a single cell.
My own front-facing reflection at arm's length — mirror wall dead ahead. The left lane with the cyan ring decals is open; turn left and advance two cells along it.
Own front-facing reflection at arm's length again — mirror wall dead ahead, both flanks mirrored too. About-face and step back one cell to open floor, then reassess.

The centered front-facing self-reflection sits one cell ahead (mirror wall), and the large clipped copy at the right edge shows that flank is mirrored too. Turn left toward the open floor with the pink markers and probe a single cell.

Open mirror colonnade ahead — the center figure is my own reflection several cells off, not an arm's-length wall. Advance three cells down the clear aisle, then quarter-turn right and probe one cell in the new lane.

My own front-facing reflection fills the center at arm's length, so this heading is a mirror wall; the clipped large copy on the left marks that flank mirrored too. The right side recedes open — turn right and run two cells down that lane.

Own front-facing reflection fills the center at arm's length — mirror wall dead ahead; the right vista recedes open. Turn right, sweep the open lane for several cells, quarter-turn right, then keep sweeping to cover fresh ground.

Front is a mirror wall at arm's length and the clipped giant copy on the right marks that flank mirrored too, so the only open route is straight back. About-face and run back along the corridor to regain open hall, then reassess.

Mirror wall at arm's length ahead on every probe here. About-face and run back down the open corridor behind, then quarter-turn and keep sweeping to cover fresh ground before the decision budget runs out.

Front and right are mirror walls at this cell; only the rear is confirmed open. About-face down that corridor, quarter-turn into a fresh lane, and keep sweeping toward the beacon with the last decision.
